title: AI Agents
question: Will AI Become Your Next Coworker?
description: After auditing time-consuming employee tasks, I explored whether conversational AI agents with distinct personalities could improve productivity while remaining trustworthy and approachable. I designed Christi and Danielle, AI assistants with access to relevant files, accounts, and information that search for answers and draft responses.

title: DeElf Tool
question: Can Design Work Be Automated?
description: Course conversion was slow and manual. I built a Node.js tool using regular expressions and web scraping to automate legacy content conversion, reducing the process from 16 hours to 24 minutes per course.

title: AI Video Generator
question: Can Anyone Make Course Trailers?
description: Creating course trailers traditionally requires scripting, editing, voice talent, and design expertise. I explored whether AI could enable instructional designers to create compelling trailers with minimal production experience.

title: Wiley Agnostic Lander
question: What Makes Forms Easy to Complete?
description: I explored how form structures affect user experience, testing wizard-style flows and Mad Lib interactions before designing a streamlined single-column enrollment form.

title: Chart.js Gutenberg Block
question: Can Interactive Charts Encourage Exploration?
description: Static charts communicate information but rarely invite exploration. I designed an interactive Gutenberg Block to explore whether animation and user interaction could make educational content more engaging and informative.

title: Social Work Degrees Redesign
question: Can UX Improve Educational Decisions?
description: Choosing an academic program is complex. I redesigned the Social Work Degrees website with custom Gutenberg blocks, clearer information architecture, improved branding, and a user-centered experience that increased engagement.

title: Preserving and Strengthening Our Culture
question: How Do You Preserve Culture Remotely?
description: As remote work became the norm during COVID-19, I explored whether an interactive React experience could communicate company values, history, and culture more effectively than traditional onboarding documents.

title: Guide That Customer Game
question: Can Games Improve Safety Training?
description: Safety training is often passive and forgettable. I designed an interactive game to explore whether gameplay, immediate feedback, and repetition could improve learning and confidence during customer interactions.

title: Sales Career Path
question: Can Design Shape Career Growth?
description: Career growth often feels abstract. I designed a series of interactive Vue applications to explore whether visualizing career progression could help employees understand advancement opportunities and stay engaged.

title: Banner Tool
question: Can Design Be Self-Service?
description: Marketing teams often depend on designers for simple graphic updates. I designed a web tool that made creating consistent, branded banners fast and accessible to anyone.

title: Shoebox Challenge
question: Can Design Bring Users Back?
description: Annual campaigns require users to return at different stages. I designed and developed a time-based WordPress experience that guided visitors from registration to shoebox reporting and prize redemption through dynamic content, automated states, and seasonal storytelling.

modalImages.caption: Each step's call-to-action (below) programmatically opens and closes based on the date and time.

title: Leading With Love
question: Can Digital Experiences Teach Leadership?
description: Leadership development is often delivered through static training materials. I designed a WordPress resource hub that made leadership content more engaging, accessible, and easier for employees to explore.

title: Wildwood Grove Interactive Tour
question: Can Maps Inspire Discovery?
description: Maps usually help people navigate, but they can also create anticipation and discovery. I designed an interactive experience for Dollywood to explore how animation and guided storytelling could enrich a theme park visit before guests arrived.

title: Shake a Sound
question: Can Phones Become Instruments?
description: What happens when multiple phones become a collaborative instrument? I explored how motion, web sockets, and collective interaction could transform individual devices into a playful shared musical experience.

title: BrowseBetter
question: Should Websites Adapt to Users?
description: Most websites present the same experience to every visitor. I explored whether adaptive interfaces could personalize content while remaining transparent, predictable, and user-controlled.

title: Parks of NYC
question: Can Cities Become Living Museums?
description: Cities are filled with monuments and landmarks with untold stories. Inspired by a museum design course at NYU ITP, I explored whether a location-aware mobile app could turn a walk through New York City into a self-guided tour by revealing nearby monuments and their history.

title: Kodi Learns to Cook
question: Can Interactive Stories Teach Life Skills?
description: Children learn best through exploration and play. I designed an interactive storybook combining games, animation, and music to explore how storytelling could build confidence in cooking and everyday skills.
